candidates.rule: The user wants the full design finished before any shop changes are made.
candidates.quote: user: finish the whole design before changing the shop
candidates.harness: Keep shop settings unchanged until the full design is complete.

candidates.rule: The initial lowest-price phase was live for a few minutes and produced zero trades before being reverted.
candidates.quote: phase-1 lowest prices were live a few minutes and reverted (0 trades)
candidates.harness: Record the zero-trade outcome and avoid treating the brief phase as a successful experiment.

candidates.rule: The design includes a three-day period at the lowest prices.
candidates.quote: 3 days at the lowest price
candidates.harness: Support a three-day lowest-price phase when the active strategy calls for it.

candidates.rule: The design includes a ledger for each customer.
candidates.quote: per-customer ledger
candidates.harness: Maintain customer-level records for the seller.

candidates.rule: Five customer types were proposed by the agent and reviewed by the user; the log does not specify their names or confirm further details.
candidates.quote: five customer types proposed by the agent and reviewed by the user
candidates.harness: Preserve the reviewed customer-type design without inventing type names or attributes.

candidates.rule: The design drops fixed opening values for every counterpart and forbids advertisements in reviews or first messages.
candidates.quote: drop fixed opening values for every counterpart, no ads in reviews or first message
candidates.harness: Do not apply universal fixed opening values or place ads in reviews or first messages.

candidates.rule: Relationship treatment is guidance in the prompt; the model chooses the amount while code enforces the limits.
candidates.quote: the model decides the amount, code keeps the limits
candidates.harness: Give the model relationship-specific direction, but enforce treatment limits in code.

candidates.rule: The user's core thesis is to prioritize exposure, spread honest information, and then adjust prices.
candidates.quote: exposure first, spread honest information, then adjust prices
candidates.harness: Order strategy priorities as exposure, honest information-sharing, then price adjustment.

candidates.rule: The market is described as an open market of opaque agents.
candidates.quote: open market of opaque agents
candidates.harness: Assume counterpart strategies are not directly observable.

candidates.rule: The Round 3 design distinguishes the rubric from the kit baseline and retains directions from Week 7.
candidates.quote: rubric vs the kit baseline, Round 3 facts, directions kept from week-07
candidates.harness: Keep rubric criteria, kit baseline facts, and retained Week 7 directions distinct in the harness.

candidates.rule: The architecture has a slow strategy agent (L3) briefing the user, market and self analysts (L2) working from epoch or slice summaries, and executors (L1) reading only the active playbook.
candidates.quote: strategy agent (L3) briefs the user, market and self analysts (L2) on epoch/slice summaries, executors (L1) read only the active playbook
candidates.harness: Enforce the stated role boundaries and give L1 executors only the active playbook.

candidates.rule: Slow strategy is user-confirmed, fast facts are determined by code without approval, and briefings and slices occur every two hours.
candidates.quote: slow strategy (user-confirmed) and fast facts (code, no approval) for L1; briefing and slices every 2 hours
candidates.harness: Require user confirmation for slow strategy changes, calculate fast facts in code without approval, and schedule two-hour briefings and slices.

candidates.rule: Restocking is an L1 agent like seller and buyer, activated by model-selected triggers; experiment fields are tracked per strategy version.
candidates.quote: restock is an L1 agent like seller and buyer (model on triggers), experiment fields per strategy version
candidates.harness: Run restocking as an L1 role with trigger-based decisions and associate experiment fields with each strategy version.

candidates.rule: The approval process has three steps and permits delegation.
candidates.quote: three-step approval with delegation
candidates.harness: Implement a three-step approval process that supports delegated approval.

candidates.rule: The memory MCP server is introduced after entry.
candidates.quote: memory MCP server after entry
candidates.harness: Make the memory MCP server available after entry.

candidates.rule: The harness uses a model-neutral system card organized in layers, with a version and intent marked for each reader.
candidates.quote: one model-neutral system card in layers with a version, intent marked per reader
candidates.harness: Maintain a versioned, model-neutral layered system card and mark its intent for each reader.

candidates.rule: Tools are exposed as JSON Schema over MCP.
candidates.quote: tools as JSON Schema over MCP
candidates.harness: Expose tools through MCP using JSON Schema.

candidates.rule: The audit agent is assigned to a model from another vendor.
candidates.quote: audit agent on another vendor's model (D29)
candidates.harness: Run the audit agent on a different vendor's model.

candidates.rule: The design supplies role objectives, trade-offs, rule consequences, and hypothesis candidates as tactical material rather than hard-coded tactics.
candidates.quote: materials for tactics instead of rules
candidates.harness: Provide objectives, trade-offs, consequences, and hypotheses as guidance while leaving tactical choices to agents.

candidates.rule: A market analyst creates a strategy profile for each counterpart, while the strategy agent maintains stances; avoiding a counterpart requires the user's decision.
candidates.quote: per-participant profiles of each counterpart's strategy (market analyst) and per-counterpart stances (strategy, delegated; avoid needs the user)
candidates.harness: Maintain counterpart profiles and delegated stances, but require user direction before avoiding a counterpart.

candidates.rule: Buyer identity must be inferred from fingerprints and confirmed after the fact, never by asking; shop-wide strategy is the default, and counterpart-specific stances apply only to confirmed or well-guessed buyers.
candidates.quote: identify the buyer by inference (fingerprints) and post-hoc confirmation, never by asking
candidates.harness: Infer buyer identity from fingerprints, seek post-hoc confirmation without asking, and apply counterpart-specific stances only when identity is sufficiently established.

candidates.rule: Deterministic metrics are evaluation tools; L1 reads only information needed for its next decision, while outside agents provide judgment-based evaluation.
candidates.quote: L1 only reads what its next decision needs, judgment-based evaluation by outside agents
candidates.harness: Limit L1 context to next-decision needs and use outside agents for judgment-based evaluation alongside deterministic metrics.

candidates.rule: Stars given by the shop are strategic judgments based on a factual baseline.
candidates.quote: stars we give are a strategic judgment from a fact baseline
candidates.harness: Separate factual star baselines from the shop's strategic star decisions.

candidates.rule: The pre-mortem calls for prefetch and tool-loop testing, stepping down under rate limits, and delegating the first briefing.
candidates.quote: prefetch and tool-loop test, rate-limit step-down, per-writer files, first-brief delegation
candidates.harness: Test prefetch and tool loops, reduce activity when rate-limited, and delegate the first briefing.

candidates.harness: Do not invent risk-limit values; obtain or load the actual limits before enforcing them.
